rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SEPARATE COMPENSATION STRUCTURE FOR THE NATIONAL PROSECUTION SERVICE AND THE LEGAL STAFF OF THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 5 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1275
rows.abstract: Section 5 of Presidential Decree No. 1275 is hereby amended to read as follows: "Section 5. Compensation. - THE SECRETARY OF JUSTICE IS HEREBY AUTHORIZED TO PREPARE A COMPENSATION STRUCTURE FOR THE NATIONAL PROSECUTION SERVICE (NAPROSS) WHICH SHALLBE BASED ON A COMPREHENSIVE JOB ANALYSIS AND AUDIT OF ACTUAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIE S AND SHALL BE COMPARABLE WITH THE PREVAILING COMPENSATION PLAN IN THE PRACTICE OF THE LEGAL PROFESSION IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR.  SUCH COMPENSATION PLAN SHALL BE SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE PHILIPPINES. THE COMPENSATION STRUCTURE FOR THE NAPROSS SHALL BE EXEMPT FROM REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6758, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SALARY STANDARDIZATION LAW."  >THE ABOVE PROVISION SHALL LIKEWISE APPLY TO THE MEEMBERS OF THE LEGAL STAFF OF THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06654

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING PROFESSIONAL LICENSE TO TEACHERS WHO HAVE RENDERED AT LEAST TWO (2) YEARS OF EFFICIENT SERVICE IN HIGH RISK AREAS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Special Professional License Privilege for Teachers in High Risk Areas." "HIGH RISK AREAS" are those places in the Philippines where terrorism, kidnappings and insurrection are commonplace. All non-licensed teachers, as of the approval of this actand henceforth, who shall have rendered a total of at least two (2) years of efficient service in high risk areas may be granted professional license.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05600

rows.abstract: This bill redefines "Philippine Overseas Shipping" as the ACQUISITION, CHARTERING, OPERATIONS, SALE OR SCRAPPING OF A SHIP TO BE REGISTERED OR ALREADY REGISTERED UNDER THE PHILIPPINE-FLAG AS THE CASE MAY BE, BY A PHILIPPINE SHIPPING ENTERPRISE FOR OVERSEAS TRADE except when the vessel is operated solely between ports in the Philippines. >The bill, likewise, EXTENDS for another FIFTEEN years the grant of EXEMPTION from the payment of income tax by a Philippine shipping enterprise.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND COMMUNICATIONS, PROVIDING FOR THE TRANSFER OF RELATED AGENCIES TO ITS JURISDICTION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The role and value of information and communications technologies in individual lives, business, and even government, cannot be fully underscored. These technologies include, but are not limited to, computers, the Internet, telephones, mobile phones, electronic commerce, convergence and other emerging technologies. Once buzzwords, these now permeate how people live, communicate and interact with each other, make a living, or do business. > The creation of the Department of Information Technology and Communications will allow the government to give due attention to information and communications technologies that will most likely eventually form the backbone of the economies of the world.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE AUTHORIZED KEY POSITIONS AND APPROPRIATE RANKS IN THE STRUCTURE OF THE ACTIVE FORCE IN THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT 8186, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Prescribing the Authorized Key Positions and Appropriate Ranks in the Armed Forces of the Philippines
rows.abstract: There is a need to increase the current authorized number of general/flag officers in the AFP due to the following reasons:  1. The present structure and future organizational structure of the AFP under the Modernization Program requires more Generals/Flag Officers in the AFP that what is currently authorized. 2. The limited authorized number of Generals/Flag Officers create an awkward situation in the AFP where the same/equivalent position are authorized different grades/ranks. 3. It will widen the opportunities for promotion of younger but deserving officers due to the greater allocation in the General/Flag Officer grades.  This will subsequently improve the morale of the AFP Officers Corps. 4. Proposed increase will further strengthen tthe command and staff structure of the AFP.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09188) enacted on 2003-02-10

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING REAL PROPERTY TAX EXEMPTION TO THE FAMILY HOME
rows.abstract: As used in this Act, the term "family home" shall mean the dwelling house where its owner and his family reside, and the land on which it is situated. A person may be the owner of the only one family home which shall be principally or predominantlyutilized for residential purpose.> A family home as defined in this Act is hereby exempt from the payment of the real property tax as long as the owner of the real property and his family are actually residing therein and the current and fair marketvalue thereof as reflected in the owner's tax declaration does not exceed Four Hundred Thousand Pesos (P400,000.00) in rural areas and Five Hundred Thousand Pesos (P500,000.00) in urban areas at the time of the availment of the exemption.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Most of the country's airports are in need of rehabilitation and upgrading to bring them at par with international standards. Inadequate infrastructure like navigational aids, airport facilities, and air traffic control services, and outmoded radar technology devices are among the aggravating factors which impeded the efficient and safe operation of domestic aircrafts needed to develop a viable and dependable air transportation network.> The continuous and growing demand for air travel makes its imperative for the government to undertake a measure that would promote a nationwide air navigation facilities modernization.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997"
rows.abstract: This bill refers to the officers and employees of the BIR. Rationale: However, much to our dismay, employment in the service of the Filipino people is once again beginning to be not so enticing. This is because some of our laws that safeguard the employment of these important resources are being mocked by some top level government bureaucrats in the guise of exigencies in service. Our laws on transfers, details, and re-assignments, are being used to serve personal interests - interests that instill corruption as well as nepotism in the very core of public service and welfare. > This bill seeks to address these issues.

rows.author: C027
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PHILIPPINE 20/20 INITIATIVE FOR POVERTY ALLEVIATION
rows.abstract: Rationale: In 1995, during the UN World Summit on Social Development (WSSD), leaders of the world, in their determination to eradicate poverty, forged a consensus to earmark at least 20 percent of their national budgets and 20 percent of Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds for human development needs. This consensus in not known globally as the 20/20 Initiative. > The adoption of the 20/20 Initiative calls for the mobilization of public resources and the re-structuring of budgets for basic social services as a major framework towards poverty eradication. At its core, the 20/20 Initiative aims to achieve universal access to basic social services, particularly basic education, primary and reproductive health, safe water and sanitatioon and nutrition.> To attain the foregoing policies, the State shall endeavor to implement the 20/20 Initiative for Poverty Alleviation in accordance with the following guiding principles: (1) Accountability and Transparency; (2) Capacity-Buildi ng;
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POVERTY ALLEVIATION since 2001-10-25

rows.abstract: There shall be established a national identification system for all citizens of the Philippines to serve as their official identification as citizens wherever they reside. Rationale: Philippine citizens do not have a single piece of an identification document that can serve them in all transactions. At present, they are required to present two or more identification cards. To institute a uniform, nationally accepted identification system this bill is being filed to solve the need.> Approval ofthis bill earnestly sought.
